principles: CPU byte order, instruction encoding order, executable file byte order, and IPC/wire byte order are distinct concepts.
Real/protected/long execution modes do not by themselves define a universal endianness policy; use the selected ISA and active endian control state.
All kernel and userspace boundary structures must declare byte order or use the canonical serialized wire format.
Never reinterpret untrusted file or IPC bytes as native C structures without validating and decoding fields.

applies_to: mobile sync manifests with binary fields
canonical_wire.rule: Decode/encode each integer explicitly; strings and byte arrays remain byte sequences.

x86-16/real-mode.notes: x86 real mode is little-endian; real-mode status does not imply the host OS can run a 32/64-bit process.

x86-32/protected-mode.notes: Little-endian integer and instruction data conventions.

x86-64/long-mode.notes: Little-endian; compatibility submodes retain x86 byte order.

arm32.notes: Record ARM architecture revision and BE8/BE32/endianness controls; do not assume all ARM32 environments share one byte order.

aarch64.notes: EL and memory-attribute/control configuration may affect data endianness; instruction fetch remains architecture-defined. Probe active state.

riscv32.notes: Current standard base profiles use little-endian memory; big-endian support is not assumed unless a concrete platform specification and backend implement it.

riscv64.notes: Current standard base profiles use little-endian memory; big-endian support is not assumed unless a concrete platform specification and backend implement it.

mips32/64.notes: Both endian variants exist; select by ELF/platform ABI and backend profile.

powerpc32/64.notes: Big- and little-endian variants exist; select by target ABI and executable metadata.

chimera-research-isa.notes: Must be specified in the target descriptor; no default is inferred from N-bit register width.

real_mode.policy: derive from ISA; x86 real16 is little-endian

native.policy: probe or compile-time select the active architecture ABI; verify against executable metadata

compatibility.policy: guest ABI byte order is separate from host byte order; use conversion at all ABI, syscall, IPC and file-format boundaries

emulated.policy: emulator models guest byte order and memory accesses; host byte order must never leak into guest-visible state

virtualized.policy: guest CPU architectural state controls guest byte order; hypervisor/device protocol serialization is explicitly defined

mobile.policy: device SoC and runtime ABI profile provide the data byte order; Android/iOS hosted APIs do not imply the same order as an emulated guest

executable_formats.ELF: Validate EI_DATA and e_machine before decoding headers; support only byte orders implemented by the selected loader.
executable_formats.PE: Validate machine and PE/COFF field encoding; executable format field encoding does not alone establish guest runtime support.
executable_formats.raw: Require an explicit signed or trusted platform profile; reject ambiguous byte order.

backend_requirements: Expose guest endian state and reset value for each supported CPU profile.
Implement endian-correct loads/stores, atomics, MMIO, instruction fetch and exceptions according to the ISA.
Test canonical LE serialization on LE and BE hosts using byte-for-byte golden vectors.
Test ELF EI_DATA acceptance/rejection and mixed-endian guest/host IPC.
Reject unsupported endian modes rather than silently byte-swapping or executing with host semantics.
status: contract-defined; per-CPU backend correctness and big-endian host CI are not yet validated
